covers: Wall Street close on 4 November, after-hours results (Qualcomm, Arm), Asia and metals on Thursday morning, and the JSE's return after the local-election holiday
headline: Qualcomm slides about 6–7% after hours and Asian chip stocks fall, a day after the Dow's best session since April 2025; gold climbs to about $4,135
summary: The JSE reopens today after Wednesday's election holiday, with gold up 1.9% to about $4,135 an ounce and the rand near R16.37/$ on Thursday morning (Reuters via Business Recorder; Investing.com, 5 Nov); early municipal counts show the DA leading in four of the big metros. On Wall Street the Dow closed up 1,569 points (+3.03%) at 53,356.12 on Wednesday, its best day since 9 April 2025, while the S&P 500 rose 1.58% and the Nasdaq 1.44% (CNBC via StockTitan, 4 Nov); Qualcomm then fell in after-hours trade on weak handset sales, and Asian chip stocks such as SK Hynix (−7.4%) and Samsung (−5.7%) followed (Investing.com via Yahoo Finance, 5 Nov). Cheaper oil (US crude settled at $88.12 after an 8% fall) and stronger metals are a helpful mix for SA miners and inflation, but chip-related shares face a weaker start.

items.title: Qualcomm falls about 6.5–7.4% after hours as handset chip sales drop 26%; Arm slips about 3% despite beating forecasts
items.summary: Qualcomm's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue fell 8% to $10.32bn, above the $10.11bn consensus, and adjusted EPS was $2.17 against $2.16 expected, but handset chip sales fell 26% to $5.14bn, short of the $5.21bn estimate; automotive and other chips rose 89% to $1.99bn. Qualcomm said it expects the smartphone market to stay flat next year. The shares were down 6.46% at 4:43 p.m. New York time (Seoul Economic Daily, 5 Nov) and 7.40% at 7:59 p.m. (StockTitan, 4 Nov). Arm's revenue rose 27% to $1.44bn and adjusted EPS was 52 cents versus 47 cents expected, but royalty revenue rose only 8% to $670m and third-quarter revenue guidance of about $1.54bn was barely above the $1.53bn consensus; the shares slipped about 3% after hours.
items.source: Seoul Economic Daily, 5 Nov 2026; StockTitan (CNBC), 4 Nov 2026

items.title: Asian chip stocks slide on Qualcomm and Arm: SK Hynix −7.4%, Samsung −5.7%, Advantest down more than 11%
items.summary: On Thursday Samsung Electronics fell 5.7%, SK Hynix 7.4%, Lasertec 12.5% and Advantest more than 11%, while Kioxia fell 9.2% after disappointing guidance. Chinese chip stocks were mostly higher.

items.title: Dow closes up 1,569 points (+3.03%) at 53,356.12, its best day since April 2025
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.58% to 7,688.62 and the Nasdaq 1.44% to 25,736.51 on Wednesday after Democrats won control of Congress and oil fell. Apple closed up 5.31%, HCA up 10.34%, Centene up 12.64% and First Solar up 4.63%; Tesla fell 3.34% and Nvidia also fell. After hours AppLovin rose 22.83% and Snap fell 11.46% on results (CNBC via StockTitan, 4 Nov).

items.title: Futures point to a mixed open: Nasdaq futures down about 1.4%, Dow futures slightly higher
items.summary: Earlier on Thursday the Yahoo Finance quote page showed Nasdaq futures down 390.75 points (−1.37%), S&P 500 futures down 0.34% and Dow futures up 0.24%, as chip results weighed on tech. These were live quotes without a timestamp, so treat them as indicative.

items.title: US 10-year Treasury yield down to 4.87%
items.summary: The 10-year yield fell 6 basis points overnight and a further basis point in early Tokyo trade to 4.87% (Reuters via Business Recorder, 5 Nov). The official October jobs report is due on Friday at 15:30 SAST.

items.title: JSE reopens after the local-election holiday; rand near R16.37/$
items.summary: Trading resumes today after Wednesday's public holiday. Investing.com's live quote showed USD/ZAR at 16.3689, 0.30% firmer for the rand, on Thursday morning. Stronger gold and platinum prices and cheaper oil are the main overnight changes for local shares; chip-linked global names were weaker in Asia.

items.title: Early municipal counts: DA ahead in Cape Town, Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni and Nelson Mandela Bay; ActionSA narrowly leads Tshwane
items.summary: eNCA's results ticker on Thursday morning showed the DA on 62.8% in Cape Town, 42.5% in Johannesburg (ActionSA 15.2%, ANC 14.7%), 40.2% in Ekurhuleni and 42.6% in Nelson Mandela Bay, with ActionSA on 28.1% in Tshwane ahead of the ANC on 27.0%. These are early, partial counts and no eThekwini figures were shown yet. In 2021 the ANC won 45.59% nationally and the DA 21.62%.
items.source: eNCA results page, 5 Nov 2026; Wikipedia (2021 result)

items.title: Gold up 1.9% to about $4,135, highest since 22 October; platinum +2.1% to $1,527.65
items.summary: Spot gold rose 1.9% to $4,134.83 an ounce by 03:16 GMT (05:16 SAST) and US December futures 1.8% to $4,144.20. Silver rose 1.7% to $53.12, platinum 2.1% to $1,527.65 and palladium 2.6% to $1,030.14, as the dollar and Treasury yields eased after the US elections.

items.title: Dollar index at 101.27, euro about $1.125; oil steadies after an 8% drop
items.summary: The dollar index fell 0.3% to 101.27 by 04:55 GMT (Investing.com, 5 Nov). Live quotes on the same page showed EUR/USD at 1.1253, GBP/USD at 1.3486, Brent futures at $94.68 and WTI at $87.54 on Thursday morning. US crude had settled at $88.12 on Wednesday after a fall of more than 8% (CNBC via StockTitan, 4 Nov).

items.title: Qualcomm (LRC Stock Scanner: HOLD, target $175.00): handset weakness hits the shares after hours
items.summary: Qualcomm closed Wednesday near $173.20 (scanner data) before falling after hours on the handset miss. A 6–7% drop would take the shares well below the $175 scanner target, which matters for the HOLD rating's upside; the scanner rating is unchanged.

items.title: Arm (LRC Stock Scanner: HOLD, target $278.60): beat on revenue and EPS, but royalty growth disappoints
items.summary: Revenue $1.44bn (+27%) and adjusted EPS 52 cents both beat forecasts; royalty revenue grew 8% to $670m and guidance of about $1.54bn was in line. The shares fell 5.28% in regular trade on Wednesday and about 3% more after hours, leaving them far below the $278.60 scanner target.

items.title: AngloGold Ashanti (LRC Stock Scanner: HOLD; JSE target R1,259, NYSE target $105.20) reports Q3 today
items.summary: Results are expected before the New York open, with consensus EPS of $1.76 and revenue of $2.89bn, against $1.32 and $2.42bn a year earlier (MarketBeat estimate). Gold near $4,135, up 1.9% this morning, is a supportive backdrop.
items.source: MarketBeat, 5 Nov 2026; Reuters via Business Recorder, 5 Nov 2026
